question.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz) \\ {x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x} & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & \frac{1}{z} \\ \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} & {x}^{2}z & \bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}\end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
question.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{y},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}yz)=2xyz,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}yz)={x}^{2}z,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}yz)={x}^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{x} & \frac{1}{y} & \frac{1}{z} \\ 2xyz & {x}^{2}z & {x}^{2}y\end{aligned}].
$$
